title: Polar Cosmogonies: Hyle, the Father's Emanations, and the Anatomy of Darkness
summary: A counter-survey alternating positive and negative cosmogonies: Hyle's self-begetting of the counterfeit cosmos as the corrupt parallel to the Mother of Life; the measure of cosmic time and the final dissolution by fire; the Father's emanations from his Five Members as the discrete-degree procession of divine articulation; the three likenesses showing First Man, Living Spirit, and Third Ambassador as one redemption in three registers; and the five bestial forms in the body of the King of Darkness as the inverted Grand Man.
organizing_principle: Alternating treatment of the two substances in their generative power: Hyle's solitary begetting set against the Father's five-fold emanation, with the redemptive operation between them and the King of Darkness's anatomy closing the section as the consummated form of self-love.
